q01.question: What is the exemption threshold for e-Invoice implementation?
q01.answer:
**RM3,000,000** is the exemption threshold. [Guideline v4.8 §1.6.1(e), p15]

A taxpayer with annual turnover or revenue of less than RM3,000,000 is exempt from issuing e-Invoice, including self-billed e-Invoice. [Guideline v4.8 §1.6.1(e), p15]

This exemption is lost if the taxpayer has a non-individual shareholder, a holding company, or a related company / joint venture with turnover of at least RM3,000,000. [Guideline v4.8 §1.6.10, p17]

q06.question: What is the Special Voluntary Disclosure Programme for e-Invoice?
q06.answer:
The e-Invoice SVDP is a voluntary disclosure programme to regularise compliance. [Specific Guideline v4.8 §17.1, p123]

It was introduced by IRBM starting from 7 July 2026 until 31 December 2027, and applies to taxpayers who have missed or not submitted e-Invoices, submitted e-Invoices with errors or non-compliant information, not submitted any e-Invoices for a period or transaction from their mandatory implementation date, or are undergoing or notified of an e-Invoice compliance review. [Specific Guideline v4.8 §17.1, p123]

Voluntary disclosures under the programme will be accepted by IRBM if taxpayers act in good faith and comply with the prescribed requirements, and taxpayers are responsible for ensuring the disclosures are accurate and properly submitted. [Specific Guideline v4.8 §17.2, p123]

For consolidated e-Invoices not previously submitted, they must be submitted by the relevant month of transaction, not as a lump sum across multiple months. [Specific Guideline v4.8 §17.6, p124]

q07.question: When is a self-billed e-Invoice required?
q07.answer:
A self-billed e-Invoice is required only for Section 8.3 transactions. [Specific Guideline v4.8 §8.3, p63]

Buyer shall issue self-billed e-Invoices for these transactions: payment to agents, dealers, distributors; goods or services from foreign suppliers; profit distribution; e-commerce transactions; pay-outs to betting and gaming winners; transactions with individuals not conducting a business; certain interest payments; and claim, compensation or benefit payments from an insurer. [Specific Guideline v4.8 §8.3, p63]

Issuance is only permitted for circumstances provided under Section 8.3, and if a transaction does not fall within Section 8.3, taxpayers are not allowed to issue self-billed e-Invoice. [FAQ v2026-05-05 §PART 2 Q20, p14]

For imported goods under one foreign supplier invoice, self-billed e-Invoice is required for each import shipment, and a final self-billed e-Invoice is required upon issuance of the foreign supplier’s invoice. [FAQ v2026-05-05 §PART 2 Q73, p29]

Are businesses allowed to issue consolidated e-Invoice for all types of transactions where

facts.text: Consolidated e-Invoice is never allowed, at any value, for these activities: Sale of any motor vehicle; Sale of flight ticket; private charter; Construction contractor undertaking a construction contract; Pay-out to winners (casino and gaming machines excepted); Payments to agents, dealers or distributors; Distribution, supply or sale of electricity (from 1 Jan 2026); Postpaid / internet subscription and device sales (from 1 Jan 2026).
No e-Invoice (including self-billed e-Invoice) is required for this transaction type: Employment income.
No e-Invoice (including self-billed e-Invoice) is required for this transaction type: Pension.
No e-Invoice (including self-billed e-Invoice) is required for this transaction type: Alimony.
No e-Invoice (including self-billed e-Invoice) is required for this transaction type: Distribution of dividend in specific circumstances (see Section 11 of the e-Invoice Specific Guideline).
No e-Invoice (including self-billed e-Invoice) is required for this transaction type: Zakat.

No e-Invoice (including self-billed e-Invoice) is required for this transaction type: Contract value for the buying or selling of securities or derivatives traded on a stock or derivatives exchange in Malaysia or elsewhere.

No e-Invoice (including self-billed e-Invoice) is required for this transaction type: Disposal of shares of a company not listed on the stock exchange - EXCEPT where the disposer is a company, limited liability partnership, trust body or co-operative society, in which case an e-Invoice IS required.

No e-Invoice (including self-billed e-Invoice) is required for this transaction type: Donations or contributions received, as specified in Question 1, Part A of the e-Invoice FAQs for Donations or Contributions.
